prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Boundary: offshore/shore wind-farm O&M; excludes public grid/unrelated port operations. Aliases: Glassfin=Turbine Controller; Morrowick=Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern=Weather Service; Juniper Vale=SCADA Gateway; Thistle Crown=Maintenance Planning Engine; Amber Quay=Shore Control Room; Kestrel Bay=Crew Transfer Vessel; Sable Orchard=Fleet Dispatch Console; Mosslight=Warehouse System; Copper Finch=Metocean Buoy; Quiet Harbor=Cybersecurity Gateway; Blue Granite=Vessel AIS Receiver; Larkspur=Blade Inspection Drone; Redoubt=Work Permit Portal; Foxglove=Emergency Generator; Wildmere=Grid Interface Relay. Other elements: Pitch System/Converter Cabinet/Nacelle Condition Monitor/Rotor Brake Unit/Turbine Sensor Bus/Main Transformer/Export Cable Monitor/Spares Hub/Helideck. Flows: Turbine Controller→Pitch Deviation Notice→SCADA Gateway→work-package flags; gateway→Session Revocation Receipt/reviewer/relay status/interface measurements. Warehouse System→Backorder Exception Slip/inventory/stock movements. Duty Planner→Transfer Manifest Addendum using Field Supervisor/planning-engine input. AIS→timestamps/Position Quality Flag→Marine Coordinator/Fleet Dispatch Console. Buoy→Wave Burst Record/local seas/offline logs; Weather Service→Squall Window Bulletin/forecasts→planning/marine planning. Weather Analyst advises coordinator; Blade Specialist reviews imagery; unsafe flights suspend; physical inspection remains mandatory. Permits: Requester→scope/location/duration/team/equipment; Duty Planner checks completeness/supply/scheduling; HSE Officer/technical reviewers/coordinator/Vessel Master review; Authorizer requires controls/reviews/bounds; supervisor checks prestart; changes require reassessment/possible suspension; team reports completion/issues; portal checked before release. Electrical: segregated transformer auxiliaries; loss auto-starts generator; transfer requires acceptable voltage/frequency; unauthorized paralleling prohibited; emergency bus excludes export, prioritizes safety/protection/shutdown, sheds overloads, alarms failures, retains uninterruptible controls. Electrical Technician verifies protection/interlocks/exercises; operators recover; planner reviews standby/corrective maintenance. Return requires stable supply/safe unloading; export restoration requires stable interface/available protections. Substation→transformer→cable→grid point; monitor measures; relay exchanges authorized signals, maintains dispatch boundary/local turbine autonomy; Grid Dispatcher sets agreement-bound requirements. Marine Coordinator maintains daily plan/resolves conflicts/distributes changes; Duty Planner

New part:
S247: The Duty Planner reviews the ranked queue and confirms that urgent work has a clear technical basis and a feasible execution path.
S248: Confirmed faults that threaten personnel safety or cause substantial generation loss receive priority over routine inspections.
S249: Planned work is advanced when its due date, condition evidence, and operational value justify the required outage or vessel time.
S250: The Nacelle Condition Monitor provides condition data that helps distinguish developing degradation from transient alarms.
S251: The Turbine Sensor Bus provides operating measurements for work that depends on recent machine behavior.
S252: The Export Cable Monitor helps planners assess whether cable condition warrants inspection or corrective intervention.
S253: The Field Supervisor checks reported faults against available evidence and identifies work that requires an offshore visit.
S254: The Blade Inspection Drone can support inspection planning when blade access from a vessel or by rope team is not justified.
S255: The Weather Service supplies forecast information for evaluating marine and aviation access options.
S256: The Weather Analyst reviews forecast confidence and highlights conditions that could invalidate a planned access period.
S257: The Marine Coordinator compares expected access conditions with vessel capability, transit time, and worksite limits.
S258: The Duty Planner considers Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, and Helideck access when selecting a mobilization method.
S259: A Weather Hold prevents mobilization when forecast or observed conditions exceed the approved operating limits.
S260: Sable Orchard assigns vessel and crew resources to approved work packages after the Duty Planner confirms the operating priority.
S261: The Marine Coordinator coordinates resource changes with the Vessel Master and affected work teams.
S262: The Storekeeper uses the exception slip to validate an unavailable part before the work package is rescheduled.
S263: The Duty Planner accounts for part availability, technician competence, and estimated task duration before committing a work window.
S264: Work packages with long lead requirements are scheduled early enough to avoid avoidable vessel standby and repeat mobilization.
S265: The Work Permit Portal supports readiness checks for work requiring controlled access or electrical isolation.
S266: The HSE Officer reviews hazards and confirms that proposed controls match the task scope and site conditions.
S267: The Offshore Substation sends a Transformer Tap Snapshot when a transformer condition review is requested.
S268: The Substation Operator confirms local operating constraints before substation work is placed in the executable plan.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
